cars.generation: Original AC/Shelby small-block Cobra roadster family
cars.variant: 289 roadster — AC chassis instruction book reference
cars.specification_market: Original AC Cobra Chassis Instruction Book reprint hosted by ChuckCobra, 65 scanned pages. First 24 pages rendered; AC/Shelby foreword PDF2, useful information PDF3 and brake instructions PDF23 individually read. Supplies untuned road chassis equipment only. Museum source separately establishes the 4727-cc Ford V8 family; its 1964 heading/1965 build label and 280-bhp claim do not authenticate a reference year or original tune. FIA 115’s 12:1/four-Weber competition engine is deliberately excluded, as are 427/428, later coil-spring 289 Sports, replicas and current continuation specifications.
cars.summary: The Cobra combined Carroll Shelby’s American V8 performance programme with the light British AC sports-car chassis. Its success in sports-car competition and unmistakable open-roadster form made the original small-block Cobra an enduring Anglo-American performance landmark, establishing a named production model beyond its Ace origins.

cars.variant: Mk I — 1960 Ural Ataman Museum road reference
cars.specification_market: Ural Ataman Museum’s own restored 1960 AN5 collection account and table provide this road reference. Native 57.82 cu in and 42.5 bhp at 5200 rpm retained without invented conversion or rating standard. No all-gears synchromesh claim is inferred from the generic synchro wording. Source’s broad production totals, launch-country claim, absolute firsts and unqualified competition victories are not imported. Later square-body Spridgets, 1098/1275 engines and aftermarket noses are excluded.
cars.summary: The original Frogeye Sprite made lightweight British sports-car design accessible through compact proportions, familiar BMC mechanicals and a semi-monocoque roadster body. Its fixed raised headlights gave it one of the period’s most recognisable identities, while the simple open two-seater established the lasting Sprite small-sports-car formula.

Cover is stamped 29 January 1963, not the index’s 30 January date. 1962 manufacture and FC1/FC1HE are declared. Selected 1147-cc base, 4.11 axle, no OD or optional servo; alternate 4.55, later OD/carbs/ratios, Mk II/III/1500 and racing equipment are excluded. No unprinted power or test performance is invented.
cars.summary: The original Spitfire brought Triumph into the accessible small-roadster class with independent rear suspension and a distinct sports-car body. Developed in response to the Frogeye Sprite and MG Midget, it became a successful British sports-car line whose original four-cylinder open model deserves its own place alongside the later six-cylinder GT6.

Factory-republished Steve Kelly/Hot Rod showroom-car assessment specifies 366-hp 400 Ram Air, optional close-ratio 4-speed/Hurst, front discs/rear drums and 3.90 limited-slip. These selected options are not described as every Judge’s standard equipment; three-speed/automatic alternatives are excluded. Native period output is not converted to modern net. cars.summary: The Judge gave the second-generation GTO a memorable muscle-car identity through functional Ram Air induction, a large rear airfoil and vivid presentation. Its 400-cubic-inch V8 and available Hurst-shifted close-ratio four-speed exemplified Pontiac’s combination of straight-line performance and theatrical design during the classic muscle-car era.
